cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: treasury bond issued 2008-03-01, first interest 2008-08-31, settled 2008-05-01, 10% semiannual coupon on 1000 par, US 30/360 basis
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 16.666667. Independently derived from the documented ACCRINTM-style day-count: serial 39508 = 2008-03-01 (issue), 39569 = 2008-05-01 (settlement), so on the documented US (NASD) 30/360 basis (basis 0) A = (5-3)*30 + (1-1) = 60 accrued days and D = 360, giving par*rate*A/D = 1000*0.1*60/360 = 16.66666667 -> 16.666667 at 6 dp

cases.description: Same terms but issued 2008-03-05, with calc_method FALSE
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 15.555556. Re-derived on the same 30/360 basis: 2008-03-05 to 2008-05-01 is (5-3)*30 + (1-5) = 56 days, so 1000*0.1*56/360 = 15.55555556 -> 15.555556 at 6 dp

cases.description: Same terms but issued 2008-04-05, with calc_method TRUE
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 7.2222222. Re-derived on the same 30/360 basis: 2008-04-05 to 2008-05-01 is (5-4)*30 + (1-5) = 26 days, so 1000*0.1*26/360 = 7.22222222 -> 7.2222222 at 7 dp

cases.description: A coupon frequency of 3 is not one of the permitted 1, 2 or 4
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If frequency is any number other than 1, 2, or 4, ACCRINT returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: A coupon rate of zero is outside the documented domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If rate <= 0 or if par <= 0, ACCRINT returns the #NUM! error value."

cases.description: Issue date later than the settlement date (arguments A2 and A4 swapped)
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If issue >= settlement, ACCRINT returns the #NUM! error value." Here issue = serial 39569 (2008-05-01) and settlement = 39508 (2008-03-01)
